test_title: PYST 25: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What was the main objective of the 4th BIMSTEC Disaster Management Exercise hosted virtually by the National Disaster Management Authority in July 2025?

options.text: To strengthen regional cooperation in early warning systems
To test joint response protocols for natural disasters across member nations
To develop a unified framework for reconstruction planning
To assess and enhance regional preparedness for cyclones and floods

solution:
The correct answer is __**A - 2, B - 1, C - 4, D - 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Nutrition Plan (National Nutrition Mission)**: This scheme was launched during the financial year **2001-02**. It was designed to provide **free foodgrains** to under-nourished groups, specifically targeting **pregnant women**, **lactating mothers**, and **adolescent girls** who belong to the **Below Poverty Line (BPL)** category. The primary **objective** was to address the high prevalence of **malnutrition** and **anemia** in **India**. Hence, the match A - 2 is correct.
 
• **Swajal Dhara Yojana**: Launched on **December 25, 2002** (falling in the **2002-03** cycle), by the then Prime Minister **Atal Bihari Vajpayee**, this scheme aimed to provide clean **drinking water** to all rural areas. It followed a **demand-driven** and **community-led** approach where the **villagers** were responsible for the operation and maintenance of the water systems. Hence, the match B - 1 is correct.
 
• **Hariyali Project**: This watershed development project was officially launched in **January 2003**. The **function** of this project was to enable **Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs)** to execute **watershed development programmes** effectively. It consolidated existing initiatives like the **Desert Development Programme (DDP)** and **Drought Prone Areas Programme (DPAP)** to promote **rainwater harvesting** and **irrigation**. Hence, the match C - 4 is correct.
 
• **Universal Health Insurance Plan (UHIS)**: This scheme was introduced in the Union Budget of **2003-04** to cater to the **health security** needs of **BPL families**. It provided **reimbursement of medical expenses** up to **Rs. 30,000** for hospitalization and even included a **personal accident cover**. It was implemented through **four public sector general insurance companies** to improve healthcare accessibility. Hence, the match D - 3 is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Watershed Management in India**: The **Hariyali Project** emphasized **water conservation** and **sustainable land use**. By involving **Gram Panchayats**, the government aimed to decentralize the management of natural resources. This project laid the foundation for the later **Integrated Watershed Management Programme (IWMP)**, which eventually became a part of the **Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY)**.
 
• **Evolution of Nutrition Schemes**: The **National Nutrition Plan** of **2001** has evolved significantly over the years. In **2018**, the government launched **POSHAN Abhiyaan** (Prime Minister's Overarching Scheme for Holistic Nourishment) with a target to reduce **stunting**, **under-nutrition**, and **low birth weight** by **2%** per annum.
 
• **Rural Water Supply Transformation**: **Swajal Dhara Yojana** marked a shift from the government acting as a service provider to becoming a **facilitator**. This philosophy is now reflected in the **Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM)**, launched in **2019**, which aims to provide **Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTC)** to every rural home by **2024**.
 
• **Social Security Nets**: The **Universal Health Insurance Scheme** was one of the early attempts to create a **social safety net** for the **unorganized sector**. It paved the way for more comprehensive schemes like the **Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY)** and the current **Ayushman Bharat - PMJAY**, which provides a cover of **Rs. 5 lakh** per family per year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Financial Contribution of Swajaldhara**: Under this **policy**, the **Union Government** bore **90%** of the total **capital cost**, while the **local community** or the **villagers** had to contribute the remaining **10%**. This was intended to instill a sense of **ownership** and **accountability** among the users.
 
• **Administrative Framework of Hariyali**: The **Gram Sabha** was empowered to monitor the progress of the **watershed works**, while the **Zila Parishads** and **Panchayat Samitis** acted as the **nodal agencies** for **fund disbursement** and **technical guidance**.
 
• **Beneficiary Coverage of UHIS**: The **Universal Health Insurance Scheme** offered a **premium subsidy** to **BPL families**. For an individual, the **subsidy** was **Rs. 200**, for a family of **five members**, it was **Rs. 300**, and for a family of **seven members**, it was **Rs. 400** per annum.
 
• **Implementation Agencies**: While **Hariyali** and **Swajal Dhara** were managed by the **Ministry of Rural Development**, the **National Nutrition Plan** was under the **Ministry of Women and Child Development**, showing a **multi-sectoral approach** to **poverty alleviation** in the **early 2000s**.
